q: A lot of scrap is re-auctioned because the first purchaser defaulted, and the re-auction realises a lower price than the original sale. The deficiency in sale value is:

options.A: Borne by the depot storekeeper
options.B: Written off without any recovery in all cases
options.C: Adjusted through the Purchase Suspense Account
options.D: Recoverable from the defaulting purchaser, as per the conditions of sale

e: Where a scrap lot is re-auctioned because the first purchaser defaulted and the re-auction realises a lower price, the deficiency in sale value is recoverable from the defaulting purchaser, as per the conditions of sale.

q: Stores are issued to outside parties and other Government departments ordinarily:

options.A: Only after the cost (book value plus departmental charges) has been deposited by the party in advance
options.B: On credit, with payment to be made whenever the party chooses
options.C: Free of cost against a simple requisition
options.D: Against the earnest money deposited by the party for stores tenders

e: Stores are issued to outside parties and other Government departments ordinarily only after the cost, that is book value plus departmental charges, has been deposited by the party in advance.

q: Dead surplus stores which have been circulated but are not required by any other depot or railway are finally disposed of:

options.A: By free distribution among the depot staff
options.B: By return to the original suppliers at the purchase price
options.C: After survey/condemnation, by sale as scrap through e-auction
options.D: By transfer to the Works Department without any accountal

e: Dead surplus stores circulated but not required by any other depot or railway are finally disposed of, after survey/condemnation, by sale as scrap through e-auction.

q: As a rule of financial propriety, Government property, including railway stores held in depots, is:

options.A: Insured with a commercial insurer against all risks
options.B: Not insured commercially, Government bearing its own risk of loss
options.C: Insured only against the risk of theft
options.D: Insured by the depot officer at his personal cost

e: As a rule of financial propriety, Government property including railway stores is not insured commercially; Government bears its own risk of loss.

q: The principal object of standardisation of stores specifications and variety reduction is to:

options.A: Increase the number of varieties held in stock
options.B: Make the procurement of stores more costly
options.C: Dispense with the inspection of purchased stores
options.D: Reduce the number of items/varieties held in stock, thereby reducing inventory and simplifying procurement

e: Standardisation of specifications and variety reduction reduce the number of items and varieties held in stock, thereby reducing inventory and simplifying procurement.

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, the 'margin of purchase preference' for a Class-I local supplier is:
e: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, the margin of purchase preference for a Class-I local supplier is 20%.

q: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, an MSE which has quoted a price within the price band of L1 + 15% may be allowed to:

options.A: Supply up to 25% of the total order quantity by matching the L1 price
options.B: Supply the entire order at its own quoted price
options.C: Claim exemption from security deposit in all future tenders
options.D: Reject the tender conditions and impose its own

e: An MSE quoting within the price band of L1 + 15% may be allowed to supply up to 25% of the total order quantity, provided it matches the L1 price.

q: The value of stores issued from a depot is debited to the head of account of the consuming department/work on the basis of:

options.A: The bin cards maintained at the depot
options.B: The priced issue notes/vouchers received from the depot
options.C: The tender notices issued for the item
options.D: The stock sheets prepared by the stock verifier

e: The value of stores issued from a depot is debited to the head of account of the consuming department or work on the basis of the priced issue notes/vouchers received from the depot.

q: The 'two-bin system' of inventory control, in which the reserve bin is opened only when the working bin is exhausted, signalling that replenishment is due, is ordinarily applied to:

options.A: A-category high-value items
options.B: Imported items purchased against letters of credit
options.C: Insurance spares of important equipment
options.D: Low-value C-category items consumed in large numbers

e: The two-bin system, where opening of the reserve bin signals that replenishment is due, is a simple control ordinarily applied to low-value C-category items consumed in large numbers.

q: Stock of an item held in a depot in excess of the maximum level fixed for it is treated as:

options.A: Over-stocking, to be reviewed for declaration as surplus
options.B: Minimum stock of the item
options.C: Dead stock of the depot
options.D: Imprest stock of the depot

e: Stock held in excess of the maximum level fixed for an item is over-stocking and is reviewed for declaration as surplus.

q: The Indian Railway Stores Code broadly deals with:

options.A: Only the purchase of stores through tenders
options.B: The purchase, receipt, custody, issue, accounting and disposal of stores
options.C: Only the compilation of stores accounts
options.D: Only the disposal of scrap and surplus stores

e: The Indian Railway Stores Code broadly deals with the purchase, receipt, custody, issue, accounting and disposal of stores.

q: Stores tenders are opened:

options.A: At the appointed date and time, in the presence of such tenderers or their authorised representatives as wish to attend
options.B: Secretly by the purchase clerk in his office
options.C: Only after the tender has been accepted
options.D: At any time convenient to the depot storekeeper

e: Stores tenders are opened at the appointed date and time, in the presence of such tenderers or their authorised representatives as wish to attend.

q: Earnest Money Deposit (EMD) is taken from tenderers in a stores tender primarily to:

options.A: Meet the cost of advertising the tender
options.B: Pay the inspection charges of the material
options.C: Ensure that the tenderer keeps his offer open during its validity and honours the order, if placed on him
options.D: Finance the purchase of the stores in advance

e: Earnest Money Deposit is taken from tenderers primarily to ensure that the tenderer keeps his offer open during its validity and honours the order, if placed on him.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Earnest Money Deposit is deposited by the tenderers along with their tenders.
2. Security Deposit is furnished by the successful tenderer after acceptance of his tender, to secure due fulfilment of the contract.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are correct: Earnest Money Deposit is deposited by tenderers along with their tenders, while Security Deposit is furnished by the successful tenderer after acceptance of his tender, to secure due fulfilment of the contract.

q: If the successful tenderer in a stores tender fails to accept the purchase order or to furnish the prescribed security deposit:

options.A: No action can be taken against him
options.B: His earnest money is liable to be forfeited, and the Railway may place the order on another firm at his risk and cost
options.C: The validity of his offer is automatically extended by one year
options.D: The Railway must pay him compensation for the trouble caused

e: If the successful tenderer fails to accept the purchase order or to furnish the prescribed security deposit, his earnest money is liable to be forfeited and the order may be placed on another firm at his risk and cost.

q: A Proprietary Article Certificate (PAC) certifies that:

options.A: The item is of a proprietary nature, manufactured by a particular firm, and no suitable substitute manufactured by another firm is available
options.B: The item is the cheapest one available in the market
options.C: The supplying firm is registered with the Railway Board
options.D: The item is exempt from inspection before despatch

e: A Proprietary Article Certificate certifies that the item is of a proprietary nature, manufactured by a particular firm, and that no suitable substitute manufactured by another firm is available.

q: Where a risk purchase is made against a defaulting supplier, the amount recoverable from him is:

options.A: The entire price paid for the risk purchase, in all cases
options.B: Only the liquidated damages for the delay
options.C: The excess of the cost of the risk purchase over the price payable under the original contract, together with other losses recoverable under the contract
options.D: Nothing, as the Railway bears the whole cost itself

e: On a risk purchase, the amount recoverable from the defaulting supplier is the excess of the cost of the risk purchase over the price payable under the original contract, together with other losses recoverable under the contract.

q: Where pre-despatch inspection is not prescribed in a purchase order, the material supplied is inspected:

options.A: By RDSO in every case
options.B: By the supplier's own staff, whose certificate is final
options.C: Not at all, inspection being wholly dispensed with
options.D: By the consignee on receipt at destination, before the material is accepted into stock

e: Where pre-despatch inspection is not prescribed in the purchase order, the material is inspected by the consignee on receipt at destination, before it is accepted into stock.

q: Stores manufactured in railway workshops and transferred to stores depots are taken into stock at:

options.A: The prevailing market price of similar material
options.B: The cost of manufacture, comprising material, labour and on-cost, as worked out through the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: The cost of the raw material alone
options.D: A nominal value of one rupee per item

e: Stores manufactured in railway workshops and transferred to stores depots are taken into stock at the cost of manufacture, comprising material, labour and on-cost, as worked out through the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.

q: Stores drawn from a depot for the periodical overhaul (POH) of rolling stock in workshops are classified under which Primary Unit (PU) of expenditure?

options.A: PU 27
options.B: PU 11
options.C: PU 32
options.D: PU 35

e: Stores drawn from a depot for the periodical overhaul (POH) of rolling stock in workshops are classified under Primary Unit (PU) 35.

q: Stores are issued from a depot to a consuming department only against:

options.A: A verbal request made by any employee of the department
options.B: A letter received from the supplier of the material
options.C: A duly authorised requisition/demand of the consuming department
options.D: The bin card maintained at the depot

e: Stores are issued from a depot to a consuming department only against a duly authorised requisition or demand of that department.

q: In the import of stores on 'CIF' terms, the price quoted by the foreign supplier includes:

options.A: Cost, insurance and freight up to the port of destination
options.B: The cost of the material only
options.C: Cost of the material plus the customs duty payable in India
options.D: Only the freight up to the Indian port

e: In import on CIF terms, the price quoted by the foreign supplier includes cost, insurance and freight up to the port of destination.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 80 lakh. If the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 15 per cent per annum of the average stock value, the annual inventory carrying cost is:

options.A: Rs 8 lakh
options.B: Rs 12 lakh
options.C: Rs 15 lakh
options.D: Rs 20 lakh

e: Annual inventory carrying cost = 15% of average stock value = 15% x Rs 80 lakh = Rs 12 lakh.

q: The AAC of an item is 2,400 units. The stock in hand is 500 units and the dues (quantity already on order) are 300 units. The coverage available for the item is:

options.A: 2 months
options.B: 3 months
options.C: 4 months
options.D: 6 months

e: Coverage = (stock in hand + dues) / monthly consumption = (500 + 300) / (2,400/12) = 800 / 200 = 4 months.

q: The average consumption of an item is 100 units per month, the lead time is 3 months and the safety (buffer) stock is 150 units. The re-order level of the item is:

options.A: 450 units
options.B: 300 units
options.C: 250 units
options.D: 150 units

e: Re-order level = (average consumption x lead time) + safety stock = (100 x 3) + 150 = 450 units.

q: In ABC analysis, 'C' category items are those which:

options.A: Are few in number and account for the bulk of the annual consumption value
options.B: Are imported items procured against letters of credit
options.C: Are safety items whose failure affects train running
options.D: Are large in number but account for only a small proportion of the annual consumption value

e: In ABC analysis, C-category items are large in number but account for only a small proportion of the annual consumption value.

q: SDE analysis of inventory classifies items according to:

options.A: Their annual consumption value
options.B: The ease with which they can be obtained — Scarce, Difficult and Easy
options.C: The criticality of the item in use
options.D: Their rate of movement from the depot

e: SDE analysis classifies inventory items according to the ease with which they can be obtained, that is Scarce, Difficult and Easy.

q: The Economic Order Quantity (EOQ) model is based on the assumption that:

options.A: The prices of the item rise every month
options.B: The lead time for supply is indefinite
options.C: The consumption (demand) of the item is constant and known, and the ordering and carrying costs are known
options.D: Shortages of the item are permitted without any limit

e: The EOQ model assumes that the consumption (demand) of the item is constant and known, and the ordering and carrying costs are known, so that the quantity balancing these costs can be worked out.

q: Stores having a limited shelf life, such as rubber goods and paints, require special watch in the depot because:

options.A: They deteriorate or expire with the passage of time and must be consumed before their shelf life expires
options.B: They are the costliest items held in stock
options.C: They can be obtained only by import
options.D: They do not require any inspection on receipt

e: Stores with a limited shelf life, such as rubber goods and paints, deteriorate or expire with the passage of time and must be consumed before their shelf life expires, hence the special watch.

q: Inflammable stores such as petrol, oils and paints are stored:

options.A: Along with the general stores in any ward of the depot
options.B: In the open yard without any protection
options.C: In the office room of the depot
options.D: Separately, in specially protected accommodation, away from other stores

e: Inflammable stores such as petrol, oils and paints are stored separately, in specially protected accommodation away from other stores, for reasons of safety.

q: Stores which are 'attractive' in nature — valuable items prone to pilferage, such as copper and brass fittings — are kept:

options.A: On open racks accessible to all depot staff
options.B: Under special lock and key, with restricted access
options.C: In the scrap yard along with condemned stores
options.D: Permanently in the custody of the user departments

e: Stores which are 'attractive' in nature, such as copper and brass fittings prone to pilferage, are kept under special lock and key with restricted access.

q: Scrap which is sold by weight is delivered to the purchaser:

options.A: On the basis of the purchaser's own estimate of its weight
options.B: Without any weighment, on a lump-sum basis
options.C: After weighment on a weighbridge, in the presence of the purchaser or his representative
options.D: After weighment at the supplier's works from which it was purchased

e: Scrap sold by weight is delivered to the purchaser after weighment on a weighbridge, in the presence of the purchaser or his representative.

q: After the purchaser of scrap has paid the full sale value of a lot, delivery of the material to him is authorised by the depot through:

options.A: A delivery order
options.B: A fresh purchase order
options.C: A stock sheet
options.D: A tender notice

e: After the scrap purchaser has paid the full sale value, delivery of the material to him is authorised by the depot through a delivery order.

q: As soon as a loss or shortage of stores is detected, the custodian (stockholder) is required to:

options.A: Make good the loss quietly from his own pocket, without reporting it
options.B: Wait until the next annual stock verification before reporting it
options.C: Sell other surplus stores to cover up the shortage
options.D: Report the loss promptly to the controlling officer/Accounts, so that an enquiry into it can be ordered

e: As soon as a loss or shortage of stores is detected, the custodian must report it promptly to the controlling officer/Accounts, so that an enquiry into it can be ordered.

q: In the event of theft of stores from a depot, the matter is reported, in addition to the departmental authorities, to:

options.A: The local press
options.B: The RPF/Police, for investigation
options.C: The firm which supplied the stores
options.D: The Stores Tender Committee

e: In the event of theft of stores from a depot, the matter is reported, in addition to the departmental authorities, to the RPF/Police for investigation.

q: The recommendations made by a Stores Tender Committee are:

options.A: Binding on the accepting authority in every case
options.B: Of no value, and are not placed on record
options.C: Recommendatory in nature; the Tender Accepting Authority may differ from them for reasons to be recorded
options.D: Final only if the lowest tenderer agrees with them

e: Stores Tender Committee recommendations are recommendatory in nature; the Tender Accepting Authority may differ from them for reasons to be recorded.

q: For certain common items of stores, rate contracts are concluded centrally by the Railway Board. Zonal railways obtain their supplies of such items by:

options.A: Placing supply orders on the firms against the Railway Board's rate contract
options.B: Inviting fresh tenders for every requirement
options.C: Purchasing from the open market at market rates
options.D: Manufacturing the items in railway workshops only

e: For common items under rate contracts concluded centrally by the Railway Board, zonal railways obtain supplies by placing supply orders on the firms against the Board's rate contract.

q: At the headquarters of a zonal railway, stores purchase work is organised group-wise, each group of allied items being headed by:

options.A: A Depot Materials Superintendent
options.B: A Senior Divisional Materials Manager
options.C: An Inspector of Stores Accounts
options.D: A Chief Materials Manager, working under the Principal Chief Materials Manager (PCMM)

e: The post of Controller of Stores (COS) is now designated Principal Chief Materials Manager (PCMM). (Source: Indian Railways tender documents, e.g. Rail Wheel Plant Integrated Bid Document 2.0, effective 01.04.2025 - 'PCMM - Principal Chief Materials Manager (earlier known as Controller of Stores (COS))'.)

q: Before an item is stocked in a depot for the first time, it is necessary to:

options.A: Sell off the entire old stock of the depot
options.B: Allot it a PL number and fix its AAC and stock limits, so that it can be stocked and accounted for
options.C: Obtain a Proprietary Article Certificate for it
options.D: Hold an e-auction for its purchase

e: Before an item is stocked for the first time, it must be allotted a PL number and its AAC and stock limits fixed, so that it can be stocked and accounted for.

q: When the equipment for which 'insurance spares' are held is itself condemned and scrapped, the insurance spares are:

options.A: Retained in stock indefinitely, whatever happens
options.B: Issued free of cost to the depot staff
options.C: Reviewed, and if they are not required for any other equipment, declared surplus and disposed of
options.D: Destroyed immediately, without any survey

e: When the equipment for which insurance spares are held is itself condemned and scrapped, the spares are reviewed and, if not required for any other equipment, declared surplus and disposed of.

q: In stores parlance, the 'stockholder' means:

options.A: The officer or official in whose custody stores are held and who is accountable for the balances held by him
options.B: A shareholder of the company supplying the stores
options.C: The purchaser who buys scrap at an e-auction
options.D: A tenderer who keeps a stock of goods in the market

e: In stores parlance, the 'stockholder' is the officer or official in whose custody stores are held and who is accountable for the balances held by him.

q: The stores accounts of a railway are subject to audit by:

options.A: The chartered accountant engaged by the suppliers
options.B: The depot storekeeper himself
options.C: The Stores Tender Committee
options.D: The Railway Audit organisation working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: The stores accounts of a railway are subject to audit by the Railway Audit organisation working under the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

q: Under the MSMED Act, where payment for supplies received from a micro or small enterprise is delayed beyond the agreed or appointed period, the buyer is liable to pay:

options.A: Nothing over and above the bill amount
options.B: Interest on the delayed payment, as provided in the Act
options.C: Double the amount of the bill, as penalty
options.D: Only a written apology to the supplier

e: Under the MSMED Act, where payment to a micro or small enterprise is delayed beyond the agreed or appointed period, the buyer is liable to pay interest on the delayed payment as provided in the Act.

q: Petty and urgent requirements of stores of small value may be met by local (spot) purchase, under which:

options.A: The storekeeper alone purchases from any shop, without keeping any record
options.B: Tenders are invited through press advertisement
options.C: A Spot Purchase Committee inspects the material available in the market and purchases it on the spot at a reasonable rate
options.D: The material is borrowed permanently from another depot

e: Petty and urgent small-value requirements are met by local (spot) purchase, under which a Spot Purchase Committee inspects the material available in the market and purchases it on the spot at a reasonable rate.

q: The re-order level of an item is 1,000 units and the re-order quantity is 800 units. The minimum consumption is 50 units per week and the minimum lead time is 4 weeks. The maximum stock level of the item is:

options.A: 1,600 units
options.B: 1,800 units
options.C: 2,000 units
options.D: 1,200 units

e: Maximum stock level = re-order level + re-order quantity - (minimum consumption x minimum lead time) = 1,000 + 800 - (50 x 4) = 1,600 units.

q: The receipt given to a supplier when material is delivered by him at a stores depot is:

options.A: Final, the material being treated as accepted at the gate itself
options.B: Only provisional; the material is finally accepted only after inspection and issue of the receipt note
options.C: Followed by payment of the full bill amount at the gate
options.D: Not recorded anywhere in the depot records

e: The receipt given to a supplier on delivery at the depot is only provisional; the material is finally accepted only after inspection and issue of the receipt note.

q: Where stores are purchased on the basis of an approved sample, the approved sample is:

options.A: Returned to the supplier immediately after the tender is decided
options.B: Destroyed as soon as the purchase order is placed
options.C: Sealed and retained, so that the bulk supplies can be compared with it at the time of inspection
options.D: Sold along with the scrap lots of the depot

e: Where purchase is made on the basis of an approved sample, the sample is sealed and retained so that bulk supplies can be compared with it at the time of inspection.

q: As a general rule, stores for the Railways are purchased:

options.A: To IRS/RDSO specifications and not by brand or trade names, so that competition among suppliers is not restricted
options.B: Only by brand names of reputed manufacturers
options.C: Without any specification, at the supplier's discretion
options.D: Only from the firm which supplied them last time

e: As a general rule, railway stores are purchased to IRS/RDSO specifications and not by brand or trade names, so that competition among suppliers is not restricted.

q: Goods and services which are available on the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal are required to be:

options.A: Purchased only through open tenders on IREPS
options.B: Purchased only from the open market
options.C: Kept out of Government purchase altogether
options.D: Procured through the GeM portal by Government buyers, as per the General Financial Rules

e: Goods and services available on the GeM portal are required to be procured through the GeM portal by Government buyers, as per the General Financial Rules.

q: The priced list of stores items, showing the PL number, nomenclature (description and unit) and the book rate of each item, is known as the:

options.A: Bin Index of the depot
options.B: Priced Vocabulary of stores
options.C: Rate Contract list
options.D: Stores Budget statement

e: The priced list of stores items showing the PL number, nomenclature (description and unit) and book rate of each item is known as the Priced Vocabulary of stores.

q: The total lead time involved in the procurement of a stock item comprises:

options.A: Only the delivery period allowed to the supplier
options.B: Only the time taken in inspection of the material
options.C: The internal time taken in processing the demand and placing the order, plus the supplier's delivery period
options.D: The time taken in the annual stock verification

e: The total lead time for a stock item comprises the internal time taken in processing the demand and placing the order, plus the supplier's delivery period.

q: Physical verification of stores is an effective internal check because:

options.A: The balances are verified by Accounts stock verifiers who are independent of the custodian holding the stores
options.B: The custodian verifies his own stock and certifies it himself
options.C: The supplier of the stores verifies the stock in the depot
options.D: The purchaser of scrap verifies the stock before every auction

e: Physical verification is an effective internal check because the balances are verified by Accounts stock verifiers who are independent of the custodian holding the stores.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 25 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 400 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:
e: Value of the shortage = quantity short x book rate = 25 units x Rs 400 = Rs 10,000.

q: Unserviceable stores which are awaiting survey and disposal are:

options.A: Mixed up with the serviceable stock in the same bins
options.B: Kept segregated from serviceable stock, so that they are not issued in error
options.C: Issued to departments at reduced rates without any record
options.D: Thrown outside the depot without any entry in the accounts

e: Unserviceable stores awaiting survey and disposal are kept segregated from serviceable stock, so that they are not issued in error.

q: Periodical review of 'dues' — the quantities of stores already on order with suppliers — is undertaken in a depot mainly to:

options.A: Increase the closing balance of stores
options.B: Fix the book rate of the items on order
options.C: Cancel or short-close orders for items which are no longer required, and thereby avoid excess procurement
options.D: Prepare the catalogue for the next e-auction of scrap

e: Periodical review of dues is undertaken mainly to cancel or short-close orders for items which are no longer required, and thereby avoid excess procurement.

q: Stock verification of high-value 'A' category items in a stores depot is carried out:

options.A: Once in three years
options.B: Twice a year
options.C: Only when the depot custodian changes
options.D: Once in five years

e: Stock verification of high-value A-category items in a stores depot is carried out twice a year, keeping in view the large capital involved.

q: Besides the programmed periodical verification of stores, the stock verifiers of the Accounts Department may also carry out:

options.A: Surprise checks of stores balances, without prior intimation to the custodian
options.B: Verification only on the request of the custodian
options.C: Verification of the personal accounts of depot staff
options.D: Physical verification of works under execution

e: Besides the programmed periodical verification, the stock verifiers of the Accounts Department may also carry out surprise checks of stores balances, without prior intimation to the custodian.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The buffer (safety) stock of vital/safety items is kept comparatively generous, since a stock-out of such items can affect the safe running of trains.
2. The buffer stock of high-value 'A' category items is kept comparatively tight, since a large amount of capital is locked up in every unit held.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are correct: buffer stock of vital/safety items is kept generous since a stock-out can affect safe running of trains, while buffer of high-value A-category items is kept tight as a large amount of capital is locked up in every unit.

q: For offering scrap in an e-auction, the arisings of scrap at depots and stations are:

options.A: Sold piece by piece, without any grouping
options.B: Mixed together irrespective of description and sold in one single lot for the whole railway
options.C: Grouped into lots of like description and convenient quantity, each lot being offered and sold separately
options.D: Handed over to the workshops for re-use in all cases

e: For e-auction, scrap arisings are grouped into lots of like description and convenient quantity, and each lot is offered and sold separately.

q: Under the Public Procurement Policy for Micro and Small Enterprises, within the annual procurement target of 25% from MSEs, the sub-target for MSEs owned by Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs is:
e: Within the annual procurement target of 25% from MSEs, the sub-target for MSEs owned by Scheduled Caste/Scheduled Tribe entrepreneurs is 4%.

q: Under the Public Procurement (Preference to Make in India) Order, where the lowest (L1) bid is of a non-local supplier, a Class-I local supplier whose bid is within the margin of purchase preference is:

options.A: Awarded the entire order automatically at its own quoted price
options.B: Debarred from the tender
options.C: Required to deposit additional earnest money
options.D: Given an opportunity to match the L1 price and, on so matching, is considered for award of the order

e: Where the L1 bid is of a non-local supplier, a Class-I local supplier whose bid is within the margin of purchase preference is given an opportunity to match the L1 price and, on so matching, is considered for award of the order.

q: Stores issued from a depot for a 'deposit work' (a work executed by the Railway on behalf of an outside party at the party's cost) are:

options.A: Issued free of cost, the cost being borne by the Railway
options.B: Charged to the deposit work, the cost being recoverable from the party on whose behalf the work is executed
options.C: Charged to the ordinary revenue of the Railway
options.D: Adjusted through the Sales Suspense Account in all cases

e: Stores issued for a deposit work are charged to the deposit work, the cost being recoverable from the outside party on whose behalf the work is executed.

q:
Consider the following statements about purchases through the Government e-Marketplace (GeM), as per the General Financial Rules:
1. Direct purchase without price comparison is permissible for purchases up to Rs 25,000.
2. Purchases above Rs 5 lakh through GeM are made through online bidding or reverse auction.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Under GFR Rule 149 as amended, GeM direct purchase without comparison is allowed up to Rs 50,000; above Rs 50,000 up to Rs 10 lakh purchase is through the lowest-priced seller among at least three manufacturers; above Rs 10 lakh, online bidding/reverse auction is mandatory. (Source: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance, GFR amendment dated 10.07.2024.)

q: Registration of a firm with the Railways for supply of stores is:

options.A: Granted for a limited period and renewed thereafter after a review of the firm's performance
options.B: Granted once for the entire life of the firm and can never be reviewed
options.C: Granted only to firms which have never supplied stores before
options.D: Not required to be recorded in any register

e: Registration of a firm for supply of stores is granted for a limited period and is renewed thereafter only after a review of the firm's performance.

q: Stores supplied by a supplier in excess of the quantity ordered in the purchase order (beyond any tolerance permitted under the contract) are:

options.A: Automatically paid for at double the contract rate
options.B: Taken into stock free of cost as a gift
options.C: Credited to the personal account of the depot officer
options.D: Liable to be rejected and, in any case, not paid for unless the excess quantity is accepted by the competent authority

e: Stores supplied in excess of the quantity ordered, beyond any tolerance permitted under the contract, are liable to be rejected and are not paid for unless the excess is accepted by the competent authority.

q: A tender which contains a material deviation from the conditions of tender stipulated by the Railway is liable to be:

options.A: Accepted as the lowest tender in all cases
options.B: Treated as non-responsive and not considered on merits
options.C: Accepted after imposing a fine on the tenderer
options.D: Held over for the next tender as a standing offer

e: A tender containing a material deviation from the conditions of tender stipulated by the Railway is treated as non-responsive and is not considered on merits.

q: Earnest Money Deposit in a stores tender may be furnished by a tenderer in approved forms, such as:

options.A: A personal cheque of the firm's proprietor only
options.B: A verbal assurance of the tenderer
options.C: Cash, demand draft/pay order, bank guarantee or fixed deposit receipt, as stipulated in the tender conditions
options.D: Post-dated cheques only

e: Earnest Money Deposit may be furnished in approved forms as stipulated in the tender conditions, such as cash, demand draft/pay order, bank guarantee or fixed deposit receipt.

q: Where input tax credit (ITC) of the Goods and Services Tax paid on stores purchases is available to the Railway, the GST amount is:

options.A: Not added to the cost of the stores, the credit being accounted for separately
options.B: Added in full to the book value of the stores in the Priced Stores Ledger
options.C: Recovered from the depot storekeeper
options.D: Treated as part of the inventory carrying cost of the item

e: Where input tax credit of GST paid on stores purchases is available to the Railway, the GST amount is not added to the cost of the stores; the credit is accounted for separately.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Stores issued to railway consuming departments are charged at the book (issue) rate of the item.
2. Stores issued or sold to outside parties are charged at the book rate plus the prescribed departmental charges.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Neither 1 nor 2
options.D: Both 1 and 2

e: Both statements are correct: stores issued to railway consuming departments are charged at the book (issue) rate, while stores issued or sold to outside parties are charged at the book rate plus the prescribed departmental charges.

q: The book (issue) rate of a purchased stores item, as recorded in the Priced Stores Ledger, normally comprises:

options.A: The purchase price alone, freight being charged separately on every issue
options.B: The purchase price together with freight and other incidental charges incurred in bringing the material into stock
options.C: The maximum retail price printed by the manufacturer
options.D: The rate at which the item was last sold as scrap

e: The book (issue) rate of a purchased stores item normally comprises the purchase price together with freight and other incidental charges incurred in bringing the material into stock.

q: In the purchase organisation of the stores department, 'progressing' of purchase orders means:

options.A: Preparing the comparative statement of tenders
options.B: Verifying the stock in the depots against the purchase orders
options.C: Following up the orders placed on suppliers, by reminders and other action, to ensure that the supplies are received within the delivery period
options.D: Progressively raising the rate payable to the supplier

e: In the purchase organisation, 'progressing' of purchase orders means following up the orders placed on suppliers, by reminders and other action, to ensure supplies are received within the delivery period.

q: Wagons carrying stores consignments to a depot must be unloaded and released within the free time allowed; the demurrage charges payable for detention of wagons beyond the free time are:

options.A: Borne as a charge on the receiving depot/stores organisation responsible for the detention
options.B: Always borne personally by the supplier of the stores
options.C: Waived automatically in all cases for railway stores
options.D: Adjusted through the Stock Adjustment Account

e: Demurrage charges for detention of wagons beyond the free time allowed are borne as a charge on the receiving depot/stores organisation responsible for the detention.

q: Stores transferred from a depot of one railway to a depot of another railway are accounted for and settled between the two railways:

options.A: Without any document, on the basis of a telephone message
options.B: By treating the material as sold in the open market
options.C: Only at the close of the financial year, in one lump sum
options.D: On the basis of priced transfer notes, through the inter-railway transfer/adjustment accounts

e: Stores transferred between depots of two railways are accounted for and settled on the basis of priced transfer notes, through the inter-railway transfer/adjustment accounts.

q: In an emergency, stores urgently required by one depot may be obtained from another depot on a 'loan' basis. Such a loan transaction means that:

options.A: The borrowing depot need never return or account for the material
options.B: The material is issued against an obligation to return it in kind or to have its value adjusted, and the loan remains outstanding in the accounts until it is liquidated
options.C: The lending depot writes off the material from its books at once
options.D: The material is treated as a free gift between the depots

e: A loan transaction between depots means the material is issued against an obligation to return it in kind or have its value adjusted, and the loan remains outstanding in the accounts until liquidated.

q: The closing balance of stores of a railway is Rs 45 lakh and the total issues during the year are Rs 1.5 crore. The Turnover Ratio of stores is:
e: Turnover Ratio = closing balance / total issues = Rs 45 lakh / Rs 1.5 crore = 45/150 = 0.30.

q: The annual consumption of an item is 3,200 units. The cost of placing one order is Rs 100 and the carrying cost is Rs 4 per unit per year. The Economic Order Quantity is:

options.A: 400 units
options.B: 200 units
options.C: 800 units
options.D: 566 units

e: EOQ = sqrt(2 x annual consumption x ordering cost / carrying cost) = sqrt(2 x 3,200 x 100 / 4) = sqrt(1,60,000) = 400 units.

q: A depot holds 300 units of an item at Rs 15 per unit. A fresh receipt of 100 units is taken into stock at Rs 23 per unit. The revised book (average) rate works out to:

options.A: Rs 15 per unit
options.B: Rs 19 per unit
options.C: Rs 23 per unit
options.D: Rs 17 per unit

e: Revised average rate = (300 x Rs 15 + 100 x Rs 23) / 400 units = (Rs 4,500 + Rs 2,300) / 400 = Rs 17 per unit.

q: The AAC of an item is 3,600 units. The stock in hand is 600 units and the dues are 300 units. The coverage available for the item is:

options.A: 2 months
options.B: 3 months
options.C: 4 months
options.D: 9 months

e: Coverage = (stock in hand + dues) / monthly consumption = (600 + 300) / (3,600/12) = 900 / 300 = 3 months.

q: The re-order level of an item is 900 units. The average consumption is 80 units per week and the average lead time is 6 weeks. The minimum stock level of the item is:

options.A: 900 units
options.B: 480 units
options.C: 420 units
options.D: 1,380 units

e: Minimum stock level = re-order level - (average consumption x average lead time) = 900 - (80 x 6) = 900 - 480 = 420 units.

q: The average value of stock held by a railway is Rs 1.2 crore and the inventory carrying cost is estimated at 20% per annum of the average stock value. The annual inventory carrying cost is:

options.A: Rs 24 lakh
options.B: Rs 12 lakh
options.C: Rs 20 lakh
options.D: Rs 6 lakh

e: Annual inventory carrying cost = 20% of average stock value = 20% x Rs 1.2 crore = Rs 24 lakh.

q: During stock verification, a shortage of 15 units of an item is found. The book rate of the item is Rs 600 per unit. The value of the shortage to be accounted for is:

options.A: Rs 600

e: Value of the shortage = quantity short x book rate = 15 units x Rs 600 = Rs 9,000.

q: Under a stores contract, stores of the value of Rs 1,00,000 remain in arrear of supply and are supplied 4 weeks late. Liquidated damages at 0.5% of the value of the stores in arrear per week of delay amount to:

options.A: Rs 500

e: Liquidated damages = 0.5% of the value in arrear per week x 4 weeks = (0.5% x Rs 1,00,000) x 4 = Rs 500 x 4 = Rs 2,000.

q: A supplier's bill for stores amounts to Rs 5,00,000. The advance payment admissible at 98% against the inspection certificate and despatch documents is:
e: Advance payment admissible at 98% = 98% x Rs 5,00,000 = Rs 4,90,000.

q: The opening balance of stores of a railway is Rs 60 lakh and the closing balance is Rs 40 lakh. The average stock held during the year is:

options.A: Rs 50 lakh
options.B: Rs 100 lakh
options.C: Rs 20 lakh
options.D: Rs 40 lakh

e: Average stock held = (opening balance + closing balance) / 2 = (Rs 60 lakh + Rs 40 lakh) / 2 = Rs 50 lakh.

q: The amount deposited by a purchaser of scrap and held under 'Sales Suspense' is finally cleared when:

options.A: The next e-auction is held by the depot
options.B: The purchaser deposits earnest money for another lot
options.C: The financial year in which the auction was held comes to a close
options.D: The material is delivered to the purchaser and the sale value is adjusted to the appropriate final heads of account

e: The amount held under Sales Suspense is finally cleared when the material is delivered to the purchaser and the sale value is adjusted to the appropriate final heads of account.

q: At the Railway Board level, the Turnover Ratio and stores balances of the zonal railways are watched and targets prescribed, primarily as an instrument of:

options.A: Fixing the selling price of scrap
options.B: Inventory control, to keep the capital locked up in stores within reasonable limits
options.C: Determining the promotion of stores officers
options.D: Assessing the earnest money to be collected from tenderers

e: At the Railway Board level, the Turnover Ratio and stores balances of zonal railways are watched and targets prescribed primarily as an instrument of inventory control, to keep capital locked up in stores within reasonable limits.

q: Under the model SOP of 2018, vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance being confined to 'A' category items, the AAC of 'B' and 'C' category items is fixed:

options.A: By the Railway Board in every case
options.B: By the supplier of the item
options.C: At the zonal/divisional (depot) level, without vetting by Headquarters Finance
options.D: By the Inspector of Stores Accounts

e: Under the model SOP of 2018, since vetting of AAC by Headquarters Finance is confined to A-category items, the AAC of B and C category items is fixed at the zonal/divisional (depot) level without that vetting.

q: Where the tender conditions so stipulate, tenderers for stores are required to submit samples of the stores offered along with their tenders, primarily in order that:

options.A: The quality and conformity of the stores offered can be judged while evaluating the tenders
options.B: The samples can be sold by the depot to meet petty expenses
options.C: The tenderers can be charged the cost of testing in all cases
options.D: The offers can be ranked by the weight of the samples

e: Samples are called for with tenders, where the conditions so stipulate, primarily so that the quality and conformity of the stores offered can be judged while evaluating the tenders.

q: Where material rejected at destination is replaced by the supplier, the replacement material is:

options.A: Accepted into stock automatically, without any check
options.B: Paid for afresh at the full contract rate in addition to the original supply
options.C: Issued directly to the user department without a receipt note
options.D: Subjected to inspection again, and accepted into stock only if found conforming to the specification

e: Where material rejected at destination is replaced by the supplier, the replacement material is subjected to inspection again and accepted into stock only if found conforming to the specification.

q: The value of stores losses, after the loss has been written off under the sanction of the competent authority, is adjusted in the stores accounts through the:

options.A: Purchase Suspense Account
options.B: Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: Sales Suspense Account
options.D: Traffic Suspense Account

e: The value of stores losses, after the loss has been written off under the sanction of the competent authority, is adjusted in the stores accounts through the Stock Adjustment Account.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A custodian of stores is not held personally liable for a loss of stores which occurs despite the exercise of due care and precaution on his part.
2. A loss of stores caused by the negligence of the custodian is recoverable from him.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: a custodian is not held personally liable for a loss which occurs despite due care and precaution on his part, but a loss caused by his negligence is recoverable from him.

q: Through the depot module of iMMS, a stores depot can:

options.A: Record day-to-day receipts and issues of stores and obtain up-to-date stock balances of items
options.B: Pass suppliers' bills for payment on behalf of the Accounts Department
options.C: Conduct the e-auction of scrap lots
options.D: Fix the selling price of surplus stores

e: Through the depot module of iMMS, a stores depot can record day-to-day receipts and issues of stores and obtain up-to-date stock balances of items.

q: Where the quantity of stores required is very large or delivery is required urgently, the Tender Committee may recommend splitting the order, which means:

options.A: Dividing the tender notice into two advertisements
options.B: Cancelling the tender and inviting two separate tenders
options.C: Placing the order on the highest tenderer alone
options.D: Placing the order partly with the lowest tenderer and partly with another acceptable tenderer who agrees to match the lowest rate, so that the full quantity is secured in time

e: Splitting the order means placing the order partly with the lowest tenderer and partly with another acceptable tenderer who agrees to match the lowest rate, so that the full quantity is secured in time.

q: A 'definite quantity contract' in stores purchase differs from a rate (running) contract in that:

options.A: A definite quantity contract has no fixed rate
options.B: A definite quantity contract is for the supply of a specified definite quantity at the contracted rate, whereas a rate contract is for supplies on demand without a commitment as to the total quantity
options.C: A definite quantity contract is used only for imported stores
options.D: A rate contract is used only for scrap sales

e: A definite quantity contract is for supply of a specified definite quantity at the contracted rate, whereas a rate (running) contract is for supplies on demand without a commitment as to the total quantity.

q: A stock item which is no longer required to be stocked (e.g., because the equipment using it has been withdrawn) is, after review:

options.A: Continued in the Priced Vocabulary for ever, without any change
options.B: Transferred compulsorily to every other depot
options.C: Deleted from the stock list/Priced Vocabulary, and the balance stock held, if any, is dealt with as surplus
options.D: Issued free of cost to the depot staff

e: A stock item no longer required to be stocked is, after review, deleted from the stock list/Priced Vocabulary, and any balance stock held is dealt with as surplus.

q: The average consumption of an item is 40 units per day and the lead time for emergency procurement is 5 days. The danger level of the item is:

options.A: 200 units
options.B: 45 units
options.C: 8 units
options.D: 400 units

e: Danger level = average consumption x lead time for emergency procurement = 40 units per day x 5 days = 200 units.

q: The minimum level of an item is 400 units and the maximum level is 1,600 units. The average stock level of the item is:

options.A: 400 units
options.B: 1,600 units
options.C: 2,000 units
options.D: 1,000 units

e: Average stock level = (minimum level + maximum level) / 2 = (400 + 1,600) / 2 = 1,000 units.

q: Items which show no issues over a long period are brought out in periodical 'non-moving' (surplus) lists mainly so that:

options.A: Their book rates can be doubled
options.B: Their continued retention can be reviewed by the competent authority and surplus/obsolete stock can be declared and disposed of
options.C: They can be transferred to the personal custody of the storekeeper
options.D: Fresh purchase orders can be placed for them at once

e: Items showing no issues over a long period are brought out in periodical non-moving (surplus) lists so that their continued retention can be reviewed and surplus or obsolete stock declared and disposed of.

q: A lot of scrap which remains unsold in an e-auction is:

options.A: Destroyed at the depot immediately after the auction
options.B: Delivered free of cost to the highest bidder of another lot
options.C: Ordinarily re-offered in a subsequent auction, if necessary after revising the reserve price with the approval of the competent authority
options.D: Taken back into the priced stock as serviceable stores

e: A scrap lot remaining unsold in an e-auction is ordinarily re-offered in a subsequent auction, if necessary after revising the reserve price with the approval of the competent authority.

q: The AAC (Average Annual Consumption) fixed for a stock item is:

options.A: Reviewed periodically and revised, where necessary, in the light of the actual consumption trend of the item
options.B: Fixed once for all when the item is first stocked and never changed thereafter
options.C: Revised only by the supplier of the item
options.D: Kept secret from the depot which holds the stock

e: The AAC fixed for a stock item is reviewed periodically and revised, where necessary, in the light of the actual consumption trend of the item.
